issue.title: Problem: no relocatable rocksdb binary in CI

repository.name: cronos
repository.description: Cronos is the first Ethereum-compatible blockchain network built on Cosmos SDK technology. Cronos aims to massively scale the DeFi, GameFi, and overall Web3 user community by providing builders with the ability to instantly port apps and crypto assets from other chains while benefiting from low transaction fees, high throughput, and fast finality.

issue.body:
Closes: #444
Solution:
- build relocatable rocksdb binary using nix
- add six rocksdb binaries to CI release flow:
  - rocksdb-x86_64-Darwin[-testnet]
  - rocksdb-x86_64-Linux[-testnet]
  - rocksdb-arm64-Linux[-testnet]

test run: https://github.com/yihuang/cronos/releases/tag/v0.0.28-test

## support tarballs

- `cronosd-tarball`
- `cronosd-testnet-tarball`
- `cronosd-goleveldb-tarball`
- `cronosd-testnet-goleveldb-tarball`

And run on different platform/arch to get more binaries.

##  package structure:
```
$ nix build github:yihuang/cronos/bundle-rocksdb#cronosd-exe
$ find ./result/
```

issue.title: Do not create duplicate draft release in GitHub
issue.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Our release workflow is like this:
1. Create a `vx.y.z` branch, then GitHub Actions create a draft release with the name `RELEASE vx.y.z`
2. In the next couple of day, we cherry-pick some bug-fix commit to the release branch as well as fill the content of the release note

The question is a new commit to the release branch will trigger goreleaser again, and create another draft release note (instead of appending to the existing one).

Seems like goreleaser only treat releases with the same tag as the same releases. While the draft release will be assigned a random tag like `untagged-1070a2429328d38d3638`.
 https://github.com/goreleaser/goreleaser/blob/f8e5bdac10a61271aee0ca58427fdb0432b3d10b/internal/client/github.go#L224-L230

### Describe the solution you'd like

Consider treating draft releases with the same name as the same release

### Describe alternatives you've considered

N/A
